findings.claim: Switching sources before either initial network phase completes drops the replacement request. The switch mutates book and reload clears detail/chapters, but load returns immediately because the old request still owns isLoading. The old request then rejects its events because book identity changed, leaving an empty new-source screen until manual refresh. An old load's unconditional defer can also clear a newer load's busy state after partial completion permits a reload.
findings.reproduction: Fake source A blocks detail and TOC. Open detail, select B while spinner is active, then release A. B engine calls never start because guard !isLoading returned; A events fail current().
findings.fix: Use a retained load task and request generation scoped to sourceURL/bookURL; invalidate/cancel the old request before clearing state and starting the replacement. Busy state writes and defer cleanup must apply only if their generation is still current. A source switch must not reuse an unrelated request's busy guard.
findings.test: Deterministic source-switch test with A blocked before first event, B succeeds; assert B is requested immediately, B content remains after A returns and only B can clear B loading state. Also reload after one A event but before the second.

findings.claim: The fast-TOC-first path is still not rendered independently. TOC success sets chapters and isLoading=false but leaves detail nil until the whole task group finishes and line 903 creates the placeholder. The body renders chapterList only inside else-if-let detail, so a slow metadata request turns the spinner into an empty body rather than exposing the usable TOC.
findings.reproduction: No cache; TOC succeeds immediately, detail blocks for 10 seconds. After TOC event, isLoading=false, detail=nil and error=nil, so none of the spinner/error/detail branches render.
findings.fix: Install the placeholder detail before starting requests, or render metadata and TOC as independent sections with separate loading/error state. A phase failure must not hide an already successful phase.
findings.test: Fake engine detail gated/TOC immediate and inverse ordering; assert TOC can be tapped and reader launched before metadata finishes, and fast metadata remains visible while TOC runs.

findings.claim: The new post-ranking generation guard fixes old-search overwrites but does not cover match-mode changes. publishIfNeeded captures exactMatch before detached ranking. applyMatchMode recomputes visible results for the new mode without changing searchGeneration. When the old exact/fuzzy ranking resumes, line 1590 passes and overwrites the newly selected mode's results. This can persist when the last publication was in flight.
findings.reproduction: Pause detached publication after it captured exact=true, switch UI to fuzzy and execute applyMatchMode, then release ranking; exact-only rows replace fuzzy rows even though the selector still says fuzzy.
findings.fix: Include a presentation/ranking revision or captured matchMode equality in the post-await guard. If the mode changed, recompute with the latest mode rather than dropping the final result permanently. Keep filter and source selection state generation-scoped as appropriate.
findings.test: Inject gated ranking and change exact/fuzzy in both directions during the final publish; verify result contents match the current selection after release and no further network outcome is needed.

findings.claim: Extraction identity tracks only the explicit extraction UUID and final URL equality, not the displayed document's navigation epoch. Reloading or replacing a page at the same URL while detached parsing is pending passes every guard and publishes HTML from the previous document. ReadableWebView has no WKNavigationDelegate to invalidate extraction on navigation start; SourceLoginWebView uses its own navigation path as well.
findings.reproduction: Capture DOM A at URL U, gate parsing, reload U so DOM B is displayed, then release A parsing. webView.url remains U and extractionID is unchanged, so article A is shown over page B.
findings.fix: Track a document/navigation revision for every attached WKWebView, increment it on provisional navigation/reload and invalidate pending extraction. Capture and check that revision before publishing parsed content. Handle same-document changes deliberately, and retain cancel-on-dismiss behavior.
findings.test: WKURLSchemeHandler/local fixtures with two responses for the same URL and gated parser; reload while extraction is pending and assert old prose cannot publish. Also test different URL, login redirect and dismiss.

findings.claim: Ad-toggle rule installation captures destination before asynchronous rule lookup/compilation. Its generation changes only when the representable input URL or blockAds changes, not when the user navigates inside WKWebView. If the user follows a link or goes back while compilation is pending, the late callback still passes and loads the captured older destination, undoing that navigation.
findings.reproduction: On visible page B, delay compile callback, enable ads blocking, navigate to C, release compile callback. Coordinator generation is unchanged and callback view.load(destination B) navigates backwards unexpectedly.
findings.fix: Associate pending installation with a navigation epoch as well as the toggle generation. On completion install rules only for the current configuration and reload the still-current request only if no user navigation superseded it; do not replay a stale captured URL. Preserve request semantics where a current page was reached via POST.
findings.test: Inject asynchronous rule compiler; toggle then navigate/goBack before completion, assert final current URL is not replaced. Test rapid enable-disable-enable, teardown and compile failure.

validated_repairs.claim: Grouped rows now use Section rather than an ordinary nested VStack, removing the explicitly eager source-group subtree.
Source kind cache now uses SourceStore.sourcesRevision rather than first/last/count heuristics.
Post-detached-ranking searchID/generation/cancellation guard now rejects results from a cancelled or replaced search, subject to the separate match-mode finding.
TOC expansion captures source/book identity and checks generation/cancellation before UI/cache writes; the original cross-source late expansion overwrite has been addressed.
Extraction now reads the mounted/current WKWebView DOM and parses off MainActor rather than loading a second hidden web page. Different final URL and explicit extraction cancellation are guarded.

Candidate roots are scored instead of taking body-first; block/BR boundaries and repeated prose are retained. Source review found no definite new SwiftSoup API compile error; native compile and fixtures remain the verification gate.
